# `@tsir/notify`

<!-- Generated by `bun src/tools/package-pages.ts --write`. Do not edit by hand. -->

## Install

After [installing the distribution](../installation.md), add this package from its workspace in your application:

```sh
bun add '@tsir/notify@workspace:*'
```

The packages are not yet published to npm.

## Example

Define a notification with the channels it sends on and a builder for each channel. Send it through a
notifier with `immediately`, which delivers inline instead of queuing. The memory channel keeps
what it was given, so the example runs with no provider.

```ts
import { createNotifier, defineNotification } from '@tsir/notify';
import { memoryChannel } from '@tsir/notify/memory';

interface Shipped {
  id: string;
  tracking: string;
}

const shipped = defineNotification<Shipped>({
  name: 'order.shipped',
  channels: ['memory'],
  sample: { id: 'ord_1', tracking: 'TRK1' },
  memory: (data) => ({ title: `Order ${data.id} shipped`, body: `Track: ${data.tracking}` }),
});

const channel = memoryChannel();
const notifier = createNotifier({ channels: [channel], notifications: [shipped] });

const report = await notifier.send(
  shipped,
  { id: 'ord_1', tracking: 'TRK1' },
  { to: { id: 'u1', email: 'ana@example.com' }, immediately: true },
);

console.log(report.channels);
```

## Failure modes

- `NOTIFY_ENGINE_UNSUPPORTED`: the database inbox was given a `mysql` connection. Its insert is
  `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, which is what makes a retried delivery a no-op; MySQL's
  `INSERT IGNORE` also swallows a truncated column and a bad foreign key, so an inbox using it
  would silently drop notifications. Refused rather than approximated.
- `NOTIFY_NO_CHANNELS`: no channels are declared.
- `NOTIFY_UNKNOWN_CHANNEL`: a channel name was used that is not declared.
- `NOTIFY_DUPLICATE_CHANNEL`: two channels have the same name. A duplicate would send two different
  destinations under one word.
- `NOTIFY_UNKNOWN_DRIVER`: a channel names a driver this build does not ship.
- `NOTIFY_CONFIG_INVALID`: a channel cannot be built from its configuration.
- `NOTIFY_NO_NOTIFICATIONS`: no notifications are declared.
- `NOTIFY_UNKNOWN_NOTIFICATION`: a notification was sent that was never declared.
- `NOTIFY_DUPLICATE_NOTIFICATION`: two notifications have the same name. The name travels in the queued
  delivery, so a duplicate is one nobody can address.
- `NOTIFY_NO_BUILDER`: a notification declares a channel that has no builder.
- `NOTIFY_INVALID_PAYLOAD`: a builder produced a payload for a channel the notification does not
  declare.
- `NOTIFY_NOTIFIABLE`: the recipient has no field the channel needs, such as an email address. A
  channel does not guess a recipient.
- `NOTIFY_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION`: the channel cannot do what was asked, such as HTML on a plain text
  channel. `only` can narrow the channels, but it cannot extend them.
- `NOTIFY_NO_QUEUE`: a notification is queued, but the notifier has no queue. Pass a queue, send with
  `immediately`, or declare the notification as not queued.
- `NOTIFY_DELIVERY_FAILED`: a channel failed to deliver. The message names the channel.
- `NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_BLOCKED`: a webhook URL was refused, because its host is not on the allowlist.
- `NOTIFY_FORBIDDEN_IN_PRODUCTION`: an ephemeral channel is used in production.

## Security notes

A notification is delivered to the recipient the caller gives it, and a channel never guesses a
recipient from other fields. Webhook hosts must be on an allowlist, because the webhook channel takes a URL
from data and could otherwise be pointed at an internal address. Webhook requests are signed, so the receiver can check
that the message came from this application. Keep recipients and content to what the user is
allowed to see, because the inbox channel stores the payload.
